minutes.headline: Board heard ARPA requests from library, food pantry and Boys & Girls Club, made annual appointments, and deferred the retiree COLA vote to next week.
minutes.summary: The Select Board interviewed appointment candidates, then heard ARPA funding presentations from the Library, the Lunenburg food pantry and the Boys and Girls Club, followed by a board discussion of the overall ARPA list. The board voted on the annual board appointments, town manager ratifications and police reappointments, took no action on Sunset Lane parking, and put the Worcester County retirement COLA vote on next week's agenda.

public_comment.topic: Resident thanked the DPW for painting center lines on town roads.
Green committee chair urged that ARPA and capital requesters consult the green committee; said state funds could cut HVAC cost and favoured solar over a generator.
Resident urged the board to vote yes on the extra retiree COLA for municipal retirees.
Resident asked for the same evidence standards for ARPA requests, questioned the Flat Hill project and opposed ARPA money for private wells.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted to make its annual board appointments, ratify the town manager's appointments, and reappoint Police Department members.
The board put the Worcester County retirement cost-of-living adjustment on next week's agenda; it must be decided by June 30.
The board heard ARPA requests from the Library, the food pantry and the Boys and Girls Club, then agreed generally to allocate some ARPA funds to most pending requests.
The town manager is to seek information from the sewer and water districts on alternative funding before any ARPA allocation to them.
The board took no action on the Sunset Lane no-parking request; the town manager is to ask police about a stop sign.

why_it_matters: ARPA money is a one-time pot, and the requests heard here from the library, food pantry, youth club and water and sewer districts compete for it, so each allocation leaves less for the others.
The extra retiree cost-of-living adjustment adds to the town's retirement costs from fiscal 26 and is retroactive, so the vote next week affects future town budgets.
watch_next: Select Board vote on the Worcester County retirement cost-of-living adjustment at next week's meeting, before the June 30 deadline.
Green committee chair's report on alternative state funding for the ARPA requests, including library HVAC.
